answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it may submit work, then assign tasks through a public lottery weighted by stake. If an agent is caught duplicating claims or colluding, the protocol burns its stake and excludes linked deposits under the same proof-of-control rules. A quill may enter through an inlet and queue at the jetty, but creating many names does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must tie up capital and risks losing it.
